title.zh: 卷三十一 列傳第一 后妃上
title.en: Volume 31 Biographies 1: Empresses and Consorts Part One
title.raw: 卷三十一 列傳第一 后妃上 Volume 31 Biographies 1: Empresses and Consorts Part One

title.zh: 卷五十三 列傳第二十三 愍懷太子
title.raw: 卷五十三 列傳第二十三 愍懷太子 Volume 53 Biographies 23: Crown Prince Minhuai

value.zh: 夫乾坤定位，男女流形，伉儷之義同歸，貴賤之名異等。
value.en: Heaven and earth fixed their stations; men and women took their bodily shapes. Husband and wife share one moral purpose, even though rank divides high from low.
value.literal: As for Qian and Kun taking their positions, male and female receive their forms; the principle of husband and wife aims at the same end, yet the names of noble and base stand in different ranks.

value.zh: 若乃作配皇極，齊體紫宸，象玉床之連後星，喻金波之合羲璧。
value.en: Those who match the sovereign on high and share the body politic of the inner palace are figured as the jade couch tied to the queen’s asterism, as moonlight married to the solar disk.
value.literal: When one is paired with the supreme apex and shares the substance of the Purple Palace, it is likened to the jade couch linking to the rear stars, and compared to golden waves joining the Xi disk.

value.zh: 爰自敻古，是謂元妃；
value.en: In deepest antiquity she was known as the principal wife;
value.literal: From remote antiquity onward, she was called the chief consort;

value.zh: 降及中年，乃稱王后。
value.en: Later ages styled her queen.
value.literal: Descending to middle antiquity, she was then titled queen.

value.zh: 四人並列，光于帝嚳之宮；
value.en: Four consorts stood side by side and brought glory to Emperor Ku’s inner court;
value.literal: Four women stood ranked together, shining in the palace of Emperor Ku;

value.zh: 二妃同降，著彼有虞之典。
value.en: Two royal brides arrived together and entered the canonical record of Shun’s reign.
value.literal: Two consorts descended together, written into the canons of Yu’s age.

value.zh: 夏商以上，六宮之制，其詳靡得而聞焉。
value.en: For ages before Xia and Shang, no reliable detail survives about how the six wings of the harem were ordered.
value.literal: Above Xia and Shang, the regulations of the Six Palaces cannot be heard of in detail.

value.zh: 姬劉以降，五翟之規，其事可略而言矣。
value.en: From the Zhou and Han dynasties on, the graded “five pheasant” ritual for consorts can at least be sketched.
value.literal: From Ji and Liu onward, the rules of the five pheasant insignia may be spoken of in outline.

value.zh: 周禮，天子立一后、三夫人、九嬪、二十七世婦、八十一御妻，以聽王者內政。
value.en: The Rites of Zhou prescribe one empress, three chief consorts, nine ranked ladies, twenty-seven secondary wives, and eighty-one attendants to manage the sovereign’s domestic government.
value.literal: In the Rites of Zhou, the Son of Heaven establishes one queen, three ladies, nine bin, twenty-seven wives of rank, and eighty-one minor wives, to administer the king’s inner administration.

value.zh: 故婚義曰：「天子之與后，如日之與月，陰之與陽。」
value.en: The Meaning of Marriage therefore declares: “The emperor and his empress mirror sun and moon, yin and yang.”
value.literal: Therefore the Meaning of Marriage says: “The Son of Heaven and the queen are like sun and moon, yin and yang.”

value.zh: 由斯而談，其所從來遠矣。
value.en: Judged by such language, their institution reaches far back into antiquity.
value.literal: From this perspective, what they derive from is distant indeed.

value.zh: 故能母儀天宇，助宣王化，德均載物，比大坤維，宗廟歆其薦羞，穹壤俟其交泰。
value.en: Hence she sets the maternal standard for the realm, advances the king’s civilizing work, and bears creation as steadfastly as earth itself; the temple accepts her sacrifices gladly, and heaven and earth look to her union with the throne for peace.
value.literal: Thus she can be the motherly model for all under heaven, aid in spreading royal transformation, her virtue evenly bearing all things, comparable to the great sustaining power of Kun; the ancestral temple delights in her offerings, heaven and earth await her harmonizing union.

value.zh: 是以哲王垂憲，尤重造舟之禮；
value.en: That is why enlightened monarchs codify law and prize above all the royal wedding rite of “meeting across the boat.”
value.literal: Therefore wise kings hang forth statutes and especially esteem the rite of the built bridge;

value.zh: 詩人立言，先獎葛覃之訓。
value.en: The Classic of Poetry opens by honoring the lessons of “Ge Tan,” the ode on diligent royal ladies.
value.literal: The poets set forth words and first praise the instruction of “Ge Tan.”

value.zh: 後燭流景，所以裁其宴私；
value.en: Dimming the late-night lamp curbs excess in the privy chamber;
value.literal: The rear candle’s flowing light is the means to regulate their private banquets;

value.zh: 房樂希聲，是用節其容止。
value.en: Sparse music in the inner rooms reins in conduct at court and couch alike.
value.literal: Chamber music with sparse sound is the means to moderate their bearing.

value.zh: 履端正本，抑斯之謂歟！
value.en: Walking straight to set the root right—surely this is what those measures intend!
value.literal: Walking upright to rectify the root—is this not what is meant!

value.zh: 若乃娉納有方，防閑有禮，肅尊儀而修四德，體柔範而弘六義，陰教洽于宮闈，淑譽騰於區域。
value.en: When matches are arranged by rule, propriety fences passion, majesty guards ritual while the four womanly virtues are cultivated, gentle models enlarge the six canonical lessons, inner-chamber teaching fills the harem, and fair fame spreads beyond the capital.
value.literal: If betrothal and intake have proper method, fences and restraint have ritual, reverently honoring ceremony while cultivating the four virtues, embodying gentle norms while extending the six meanings, then women’s instruction permeates the palace, and good reputation rises through the regions.

value.zh: 則玄雲入戶，上帝錫母萌之符；
value.en: Then auspicious clouds cross the threshold and Heaven grants the token of fruitful motherhood;
value.literal: Then dark clouds enter the door, and the Supreme Lord grants the sign of motherhood’s sprouting;

value.zh: 黃神降徵，坤靈贊壽丘之道，終能鼎祚惟永，胤嗣克昌。
value.en: The divine Yellow Emperor sends portents; earth’s spirit blesses the birth-hill of sage-kings; the dynasty’s mandate endures and heirs thrive.
value.literal: The Yellow Spirit sends down omens; the spirit of Kun assists the way of Shouqiu; ultimately the tripod fortune can be everlasting and heirs flourish.

value.zh: 至若儷極虧閑，憑天作孽，倒裳衣于衽席，感朓側於弦望。
value.en: But women who reach the throne yet abandon modesty, who invoke Heaven while plotting harm, who turn proper dress upside down on the bed, and whose passions shift with every phase of the moon—
value.literal: As for those paired to the apex yet deficient in restraint, who rely on heaven to work calamity, who overturn upper and lower garments upon the mat, and feel lust askew at first quarter and full moon.

value.zh: 則龍漦結釁，宗周鞠為黍苗；
value.en: —dragon spit seals a fatal feud, and the Zhou heartland turns to weed-grown ruin;
value.literal: Then dragon-spittle knots disaster, and royal Zhou becomes nothing but millet shoots;

value.zh: 燕尾挻災，隆漢墜其枌社矣。
value.en: swallow-tail charms invite catastrophe, and even mighty Han loses its soil-and-millet shrines.
value.literal: Swallow tails draw calamity, and flourishing Han drops its mulberry altars.

value.zh: 自曹劉內主，位以色登，甄衛之家，榮非德舉。
value.en: Under the Cao and Liu courts, palace ladies rose by looks alone; clans such as the Zhens and Weis won favor without moral merit.
value.literal: Since the inner mistresses of Cao and Liu, position climbed by beauty; in the households of Zhen and Wei, glory was not raised by virtue.

value.zh: 淫荒挺性，蔑西郊之禮容；
value.en: Wanton temperaments mocked the solemn suburban liturgy reserved for the empress;
value.literal: Dissolute and wasteful by nature, they slighted the ritual bearing of the western suburb;

value.zh: 婉孌含辭，作南國之奇態。
value.en: Soft voices and studied phrases invented the freakish grace of southern entertainers.
value.literal: Soft loveliness holding coy phrases, they fashioned exotic manners of the southern states.

value.zh: 詖謁由斯外人，穢德於是內宣。
value.en: Sycophancy leaked beyond the palace gates while depravity was preached inside.
value.literal: Slanderous flattery thereby passed outward, and foul conduct was proclaimed within.

value.zh: 椒掖播晨牝之風，蘭殿絕河雎之響。
value.en: The harem aired the omen of women ruling like crowing hens; orchid halls no longer echoed the chaste songs of “Guan ju.”
value.literal: The pepper chambers spread the wind of the hen crowing at dawn; the orchid halls cut off the echo of “Guan ju” by the River.

value.zh: 永言彤史，大練之範逾微；
value.en: Forever the palace diarists wrote, yet the ideal of homespun austerity faded;
value.literal: Speaking long of the vermilion scribe, the model of coarse white silk grows ever fainter;

value.zh: 緬視青蒲，脫珥之猷替矣。
value.en: Looking back to mat audiences where consorts remonstrated, the counsel of tearing off earrings to warn the throne had vanished.
value.literal: Gazing afar at the green rushes, the strategy of casting off ear-jewels is replaced.

value.zh: 晉承其末，與世污隆，宣皇創基，功弘而道屈；
value.en: The Jin took up this fallen era and rose or fell with the times. Emperor Xuan laid the foundations: his deeds were grand, yet the moral course stayed cramped;
value.literal: Jin inherited the late age; with the world it sank and rose. Emperor Xuan founded the base—achievement broad yet the Way bent;

value.zh: 穆后一善，勣侔於十亂。
value.en: a single virtue in Empress Mu rivaled the merit of the “ten turbulent” worthies who saved a dynasty.
value.literal: one goodness of Empress Mu—merit equal to the Ten Disorderly Ones.

value.zh: 洎乎世祖，[1]始親選良家，既而帝掩紈扇，躬行請託。
value.en: Under Emperor Wu [1] the court at first picked brides from respectable houses; soon the sovereign waved his silk fan in the inner quarters and himself traded favors for appointments.
value.literal: Down to Shizu [1], he began personally selecting from good families; thereafter the emperor hid behind the silk fan and personally practiced solicitation.

value.zh: 后採長白，實彰妒忌之情；
value.en: An empress chosen for graying hair laid bare the spite of jealousy;
value.literal: The empress chose “long white,” truly displaying jealousy;

value.zh: 賈納短青，竟踐覆亡之轍。
value.en: the Jias welcomed a young rival and eventually followed the same rut to ruin.
value.literal: Jia took in “short green,” and in the end trod the rut of overthrow.

value.zh: 得失遺跡，煥在綈緗，興滅所由，義同畫一。
value.en: Success and failure still gleam from the silk-bound histories; the springs of fortune and disaster follow one clear pattern.
value.literal: Tracks of gain and loss shine forth on silk documents; the causes of rise and ruin share one uniform pattern in meaning.

value.zh: 故列其本事，以為后妃傳云。
value.en: I therefore set out the essential facts as this “Treatise on Empresses and Consorts.”
value.literal: Therefore I array their basic affairs to form this treatise on empresses and consorts.

value.zh: 惠賈皇后諱南風，平陽人也，小名時。
value.en: Empress Jia Nanfeng of Pingyang—pet name Shi.
value.literal: Empress Jia of Hui, taboo Nanfeng, native of Pingyang, childhood name Shi.

value.zh: 父充，別有傳。
value.en: Her father Jia Chong has his own biography.
value.literal: Her father Chong has separate biography.

value.zh: 初，武帝欲為太子取衛瓘女，元后納賈郭親黨之說，欲婚賈氏。
value.en: Wu favored Wei Guan’s daughter; Empress Yang Yan pushed Jia kin.
value.literal: At first Emperor Wu wished crown prince to marry Wei Guan’s daughter; Empress Yuan listened to Jia and Guo faction urging marriage with Jia clan.

value.zh: 帝曰：「衛公女有五可，賈公女有五不可。
value.en: Wu said, “Wei’s girl scores five merits—Jia’s five flaws.
value.literal: Emperor said: “Lord Wei’s daughter has five goods—Lord Jia’s daughter five bads.

value.zh: 衛家種賢而多子，美而長白；
value.en: Weis are fertile and wise—fair and statuesque;
value.literal: Wei house breeds wise and many sons—beautiful, tall, fair;

value.zh: 賈家種妒而少子，醜而短黑。」
value.en: Jias are jealous and barren—dark and squat."
value.literal: Jia house breeds jealousy and few sons—ugly, short, dark.”

value.zh: 元后固請，荀顗、荀勖並稱充女之賢，乃定婚。
value.en: Yang Yan insisted; Xun Yi and Xun Xu praised Jia’s girl—the match closed.
value.literal: Empress Yuan pressed firmly—Xun Yi and Xun Xu together praised Chong’s daughter’s virtue—betrothal fixed.

value.zh: 始欲聘后妹午，午年十二，小太子一歲，短小未勝衣。
value.en: They first chose sister Wu—twelve, petite beside the heir.
value.literal: At first they wished to engage younger sister Wu—Wu twelve years old, one year younger than crown prince, too short for robes.

value.zh: 更娶南風，時年十五，大太子二歲。
value.en: They wed Nanfeng instead—fifteen, two years his senior.
value.literal: They switched to Nanfeng—then fifteen, two years elder than crown prince.

value.zh: 泰始八年二月辛卯[7]，冊拜太子妃。
value.en: On xinmao in early 272 she became crown princess [7].
value.literal: Eighth Taishi year second month xinmao [7]—invested crown princess.

value.zh: 妒忌多權詐，太子畏而惑之，嬪御罕有進幸者。
value.en: Jealous and scheming, she cowed the befuddled prince—other women seldom touched him.
value.literal: Jealous, crafty in intrigue—crown prince feared yet dazed—concubines rarely gained favor.

value.zh: 初，后詐有身，內稿物為產具，遂取妹夫韓壽子慰祖養之，託諒闇所生，故弗顯。
value.en: She faked pregnancy—snatched Han Shou’s son Weizu—called him newborn heir.
value.literal: At first consort feigned pregnancy—packed straw goods as birthing gear—then took sister’s husband Han Shou’s son Weizu raising—claimed mourning-hall birth—therefore not openly shown.

value.zh: 遂謀廢太子，以所養代立。
value.en: She meant to replace the heir with him.
value.literal: Then plotted depose crown prince—establish fosterling.

value.zh: 時洛中謠曰：「南風烈烈吹黃沙，遙望魯國鬱嵯峨，前至三月滅汝家。」
value.en: Luoyang sang: "Nanfeng blasts yellow dust—far off Lu towers loom—by the third moon your house will fall."
value.literal: Then Luoyang rhyme said: "South wind fierce blows yellow sand—far gaze Lu kingdom towering—before third month ends your house."

value.zh: 后母廣城君以后無子，甚敬重愍懷，每勸厲后，使加慈愛。
value.en: Lady Guo prized Minhuai—begged Jia to cherish him.
value.literal: Consort mother Lady Guangcheng because consort lacked sons greatly revered Crown Prince Minhuai—often urged consort—made her add kindness.

value.zh: 賈謐恃貴驕縱，不能推崇太子，廣城君恒切責之。
value.en: Jia Mi insulted the heir—Lady Guo scolded him.
value.literal: Jia Mi relied on pride—could not honor crown prince—Lady Guangcheng constantly scolded.

value.zh: 及廣城君病篤，占術謂不宜封廣城，乃改封宜城。
value.en: Ill diviners forbade “Guangcheng”—she became Princess Yicheng.
value.literal: When Lady Guangcheng gravely ill—divination said unsuitable enfeoff Guangcheng—thereupon changed enfeoff Yicheng.

value.zh: 后出侍疾十餘日，太子常往宜城第，將醫出入，恂恂盡禮。
value.en: Minhuai nursed her mother—deferential.
value.literal: Consort attended illness ten-plus days—crown prince often visited Yicheng mansion—brought physicians—obedient exhaustive ritual.

value.zh: 宜城臨終執后手，令盡意于太子，言甚切至。
value.en: She clasped Jia’s hand—beg her shield Minhuai.
value.literal: Yicheng dying grasped consort’s hand—ordered exhaust feeling toward crown prince—speech extremely earnest.

value.zh: 又曰：「趙粲及午必亂汝事，我死後，勿復聽入，深憶吾言。」
value.en: She also said, "Zhao Can and Jia Wu will surely disrupt your affairs; after I die, do not admit them again—remember my words well."
value.literal: Also said: “Zhao Can and Wu surely ruin your affairs—after I die—never hear them again—deeply remember my words.”

value.zh: 后不能遵之，遂專制天下，威服內外。
value.en: Jia ignored—ruled alone.
value.literal: Consort could not obey—thereupon monopolized realm—awe subdued inner and outer.

value.zh: 更與粲、午專為姦謀，誣害太子，眾惡彰著。
value.en: She schemed with them against Minhuai.
value.literal: Further with Can, Wu solely plotted wickedness—slandered harmed crown prince—crowds of evils manifest.

value.zh: 初，誅楊駿及汝南王亮、太保衛瓘、楚王瑋等，皆臨機專斷，宦人董猛參預其事。
value.en: Yang Jun, Sima Liang, Wei Guan, Sima Wei died by her whim—with eunuch Dong Meng.
value.literal: At first executing Yang Jun and Prince Runan Liang, Grand Tutor Wei Guan, Prince Chu Wei—all improvised executions—eunuch Dong Meng participated.

value.zh: 猛，武帝時為寺人監，侍東宮，得親信于后，預誅楊駿，封武安侯，猛三兄皆為亭侯，天下咸怨。
value.en: Dong Meng gained titles—his brothers too—the realm cursed them.
value.literal: Meng—Wu-era Inner Palace Overseer—served Eastern Palace—won consort trust—participated executing Yang Jun—enfeoffed Marquis Wu’an—Meng three elder brothers all village marquis—all realm resented.

value.zh: 及太子廢黜，趙王倫、孫秀等因眾怨謀欲廢后[8]。
value.en: Once Minhuai fell Sima Lun and Sun Xiu used hatred to target her [8].
value.literal: When crown prince deposed—Prince Zhao Lun and Sun Xiu exploiting resentment plotted depose consort [8].

value.zh: 后數遣宮婢微服於人間視聽，其謀頗泄。
value.en: She spied on rumors—some leaked.
value.literal: Consort repeatedly sent palace maids plain clothes among folk spy listen—plot leaked somewhat.

value.zh: 后甚懼，遂害太子，以絕眾望。
value.en: Terrified she murdered Minhuai.
value.literal: Consort greatly afraid—thereupon harmed crown prince—cutting off hopes.

value.zh: 趙王倫乃率兵入宮，使翊軍校尉齊王冏入殿廢后。
value.en: Sima Lun stormed in—sent Sima Jiong to drag her out.
value.literal: Prince Zhao Lun then led troops palace—ordered Colonel Qi Wang Jiong enter hall depose consort.

value.zh: 后與冏母有隙，故倫使之。
value.en: Jiong hated her mother—Lun used him.
value.literal: Consort with Jiong’s mother bore grudge—therefore Lun sent him.

value.zh: 后驚曰：「卿何為來！」
value.en: She cried, “Why you!”
value.literal: Consort alarmed said: “Why have you come!”

value.zh: 冏曰：「有詔收后。」
value.en: Jiong said, "There is an edict to seize you."
value.literal: Jiong said: "There is an edict to seize you."

value.zh: 后曰：「詔當從我出，何詔也？」
value.en: She snapped, "Edicts issue from me—what edict is this?"
value.literal: Consort said: "Edicts issue from me—what edict is this?"

value.zh: 后至上閤，遙呼帝曰：「陛下有婦，使人廢之，亦行自廢。」
value.en: Reaching the upper chamber she cried to the emperor, "Your Majesty has a wife, yet you let others depose her—you will be deposed yourself."
value.literal: Consort reaching upper chamber cried distant emperor: “Your Majesty has wife yet lets others depose her—you yourself will be deposed.”

value.zh: 又問冏曰：「起事者誰？」
value.en: She asked Jiong again, "Who raised this affair?"
value.literal: Again asked Jiong: “Who raised revolt?”

value.zh: 冏曰：「梁、趙。」
value.en: “Liang and Zhao.”
value.literal: Jiong said: “Liang and Zhao.”

value.zh: 后曰：「繫狗當繫頸，今反繫其尾，何得不然！」
value.en: “Chain a dog by the throat—you seized the tail—no wonder!”
value.literal: Consort said: “Leash dog by throat—now leash tail—how can it not be so!”

value.zh: 至宮西，見謐尸，再舉聲而哭遽止。
value.en: Seeing Jia Mi’s corpse she wailed twice—then silence.
value.literal: Reaching palace west saw Mi corpse—raised voice twice weeping suddenly stopped.

value.zh: 倫乃矯詔遣尚書劉弘等持節齎金屑酒賜后死。
value.en: Sima Lun sent Liu Hong with golden liquor.
value.literal: Lun then forged edict dispatch Minister Liu Hong bearing tally deliver gold-filings wine grant consort death.

value.zh: 后在位十一年。
value.en: Eleven years queen.
value.literal: Consort held rank eleven years.

value.zh: 趙粲、賈午、韓壽、董猛等皆伏誅。
value.en: Her cabal died with her.
value.literal: Zhao Can, Jia Wu, Han Shou, Dong Meng executed.

value.zh: 愍懷太子
value.en: Crown Prince Minhuai
value.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai

value.zh: 太子性剛，知賈謐恃後之貴，不能假借之。
value.en: Yu refused to flatter Jia Mi.
value.literal: The crown prince's temper was stiff; knowing Jia Mi relied on the empress's power, he would not indulge him.

value.zh: 謐至東宮，或舍之而於後庭遊戲。
value.en: He left Jia Mi cooling heels while he played inside.
value.literal: When Mi came to the Eastern Palace he sometimes left him waiting while he played in the inner courts.

value.zh: 詹事裴權諫曰：「賈謐甚有寵于中宮，而有不順之色，若一旦交構，大事去矣。
value.en: Household Superintendent Pei Quan remonstrated: "Jia Mi is deeply favored in the inner palace yet shows disrespectful looks—if they ever turn on you, the great enterprise is lost.
value.literal: Household Superintendent Pei Quan remonstrated: 'Jia Mi is deeply favored in the inner palace yet shows disrespectful looks—if they ever turn on you, the great enterprise is lost.

value.zh: 宜深自謙屈，以防其變，廣延賢士，用自輔翼。」
value.en: You should humble yourself deeply to guard against change and broadly recruit worthy men to aid your wings."
value.literal: You should humble yourself deeply to guard against change and broadly recruit worthy men to aid your wings.'

value.zh: 太子不能從。
value.en: Yu ignored him.
value.literal: The crown prince would not follow.

value.zh: 初，賈后母郭槐欲以韓壽女為太子妃，太子亦欲婚韓氏以自固。
value.en: Guo Huai once pushed a Han match—Yu wanted it too.
value.literal: Earlier Empress Jia's mother Guo Huai had wished to take Han Shou's daughter as crown princess; the crown prince also wished to marry the Hans to strengthen himself.

value.zh: 而壽妻賈午及後皆不聽，而為太子聘王衍小女惠風。
value.en: Jia Wu and the empress forced Wang Yan's younger daughter Huifeng instead.
value.literal: But Han Shou's wife Jia Wu and the empress both refused and instead betrothed the crown prince to Wang Yan's younger daughter Huifeng.

value.zh: 太子聞衍長女美，而賈后為謐聘之，心不能平，頗以為言。
value.en: Yu resented losing Wang's elder beauty to Jia Mi.
value.literal: The crown prince heard Wang's elder daughter was beautiful while the empress betrothed her to Jia Mi; his heart could not rest easy and he spoke of it often.

value.zh: 謐嘗與太子圍棋，爭道，成都王穎見而訶謐，謐意愈不平，因此譖太子于後曰：「太子廣買田業，多畜私財以結小人者，為賈氏故也。
value.en: Once while playing go with the crown prince Mi quarreled over a move; Ying, Prince of Chengdu, saw and rebuked Mi; Mi grew more resentful and slandered the crown prince to the empress: "The crown prince buys fields wholesale, hoards private wealth, and courts petty men—all because of the Jia clan.
value.literal: Once Mi played go with the crown prince and they quarreled over the move; Ying, Prince of Chengdu, saw and rebuked Mi; Mi grew more resentful and therefore slandered the crown prince to the empress: 'The crown prince buys fields wholesale, hoards private wealth, and courts petty men—all because of the Jia clan.

value.zh: 密聞其言云：'皇后萬歲後，吾當魚肉之。
value.en: Mi quoted Yu vowing to slaughter the Jias after Jia died.
value.literal: I have secretly heard him say: "After the empress dies, I shall butcher them."

value.zh: '非但如是也，若宮車晏駕，彼居大位，依楊氏故事，誅臣等而廢後於金墉，如反手耳。
value.en: Not only that—if the imperial carriage halts and he reaches the great seat, following Lady Yang's precedent he will execute us ministers and lock you away at Jinyong like turning his hand.
value.literal: Not only that—if the imperial carriage halts and he reaches the great seat, following Lady Yang's precedent he will execute us ministers and lock you away at Jinyong like turning his hand.

value.zh: 不如早為之所，更立慈順者以自防衛。」
value.en: Better strike early, remove him, and set up someone kindly and tractable to defend ourselves."
value.literal: Better strike early, remove him, and set up someone kindly and tractable to defend ourselves.'

value.zh: 後納其言，又宣揚太子之短，布諸遠近。
value.en: Jia adopted the plot and smeared Yu empire-wide.
value.literal: The empress accepted his words and further broadcast the crown prince's faults throughout near and far.

value.zh: 于時朝野咸知賈后有害太子意。
value.en: Everyone saw Jia meant to kill the heir.
value.literal: Then court and countryside knew the empress meant to harm the crown prince.

value.zh: 中護軍趙俊請太子廢後，太子不聽。
value.en: Zhao Jun urged preemptive deposition—Yu declined.
value.literal: Central Guard Zhao Jun asked the crown prince to depose the empress first; the crown prince refused.

value.zh: 資治通鑑第083卷
value.en: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 83
value.literal: Comprehensive Mirror to Aid in Government, Volume 83

value.zh: 初，廣城君郭槐，以賈后無子，常勸后使慈愛太子。
value.en: Earlier Guo Huai, Lady of Guangcheng, because Empress Jia had no son of her own, often urged her to treat the heir apparent kindly.
value.literal: Earlier the Lady of Guangcheng, Guo Huai, because Empress Jia had no son, often urged the empress to treat the Heir Apparent with kindness.

value.zh: 賈謐驕縱，數無禮於太子，廣城君恆切責之。
value.en: Jia Mi was arrogant and repeatedly insulted the heir apparent. The Lady of Guangcheng scolded him harshly again and again.
value.literal: Jia Mi was arrogant and unrestrained, repeatedly disrespectful toward the Heir Apparent; the Lady of Guangcheng constantly rebuked him sharply.

value.zh: 廣城君欲以韓壽女為太子妃，太子亦欲婚韓氏以自固；
value.en: The Lady of Guangcheng wanted Han Shou's daughter as the heir apparent's consort, and the heir apparent likewise hoped to marry into the Han clan to strengthen his position;
value.literal: The Lady of Guangcheng wished to make Han Shou's daughter the Heir Apparent's consort; the Heir Apparent also wished to marry into the Han clan to secure himself;

value.zh: 壽妻賈午及后皆不聽，而為太子聘王衍少女。
value.en: but Han Shou's wife Jia Wu and the empress refused and betrothed the heir apparent to Wang Yan's younger daughter instead.
value.literal: Han Shou's wife Jia Wu and the empress would not agree, and instead betrothed to the Heir Apparent the younger daughter of Wang Yan.

value.zh: 太子聞衍長女美，而后為賈謐聘之，心不能平，頗以為言。
value.en: The heir apparent heard that Yan's elder daughter was beautiful, yet the empress gave her to Jia Mi. He was bitter and complained openly.
value.literal: The Heir Apparent heard that Yan's elder daughter was beautiful, yet the empress betrothed her to Jia Mi; he could not compose his heart and spoke of it with some resentment.

value.zh: 及廣城君病，臨終，執后手，令盡心於太子，言甚切至。
value.en: When the Lady of Guangcheng fell mortally ill, she took the empress's hand at the end and urged her with utmost earnestness to devote herself to the heir apparent.
value.literal: When the Lady of Guangcheng fell ill, at the end she took the empress's hand and ordered her to devote her heart to the Heir Apparent, her words very earnest.

value.zh: 又曰：「趙粲、賈午，必亂汝家事；
value.en: She also said: "Zhao Can and Jia Wu will surely ruin your household.
value.literal: She also said: "Zhao Can and Jia Wu will surely ruin your household affairs;

value.zh: 我死後，勿復聽入。
value.en: After I die, do not let them near you again.
value.literal: after my death, do not again let them enter your counsel.

value.zh: 深記吾言。」
value.en: Remember this well."
value.literal: Remember my words deeply."

value.zh: 后不從，更與粲、午謀害太子。
value.en: The empress ignored her and instead joined Can and Wu in plotting against the heir apparent.
value.literal: The empress did not obey and instead joined with Can and Wu to plot harm to the Heir Apparent.

value.zh: 趙王倫、孫秀將討賈后，告右衛佽飛督閭和，和從之，期以癸巳丙夜一籌，以鼓聲為應。
value.en: Lun and Xiu prepared to move against the empress, won over Lü He, Colonel of the Right Guards Attendants, and set guisi night, second watch of the bing hour, drums as signal.
value.literal: The Prince of Zhao Lun and Sun Xiu were about to attack Empress Jia; they told the Colonel of the Right Guards Attendants Lü He, who joined them, fixing the night of guisi on the second watch of the bing hour, with drumbeats as signal.

value.zh: 癸巳，秀使司馬雅告張華曰：「趙王欲與公共匡社稷，為天下除害，使雅以告。」
value.en: On guisi Xiu had Sima Ya tell Zhang Hua: "The Prince of Zhao wishes to join you to save the realm and remove this evil."
value.literal: On guisi Xiu had Sima Ya tell Zhang Hua: "The Prince of Zhao wishes to join with you to steady the altars, remove harm for the realm—Ya reports this."

value.zh: 華拒之。
value.en: Hua refused.
value.literal: Hua refused.

value.zh: 雅怒曰：「刃將加頸，猶為是言邪！」
value.en: Ya snapped: "The blade is at your neck and you still talk like that!"
value.literal: Ya angrily said: "The blade is at the neck—yet you speak thus!"

value.zh: 不顧而出。
value.en: He strode out without a backward glance.
value.literal: He left without looking back.

value.zh: 及期，倫矯詔敕三部司馬曰：「中宮與賈謐等殺吾太子，今使車騎入廢中宮，汝等皆當從命，事畢，賜爵關中侯，不從者誅三族。」
value.en: At the hour Lun forged an edict to the three departments: "The empress and Jia Mi killed the heir apparent. The Cavalry General enters to depose her. Obey and receive marquisates; disobey and face extermination."
value.literal: When the hour came Lun forged an edict instructing the three departments' majors: "The central palace and Jia Mi and others killed our Heir Apparent; the Cavalry General will enter and depose the central palace—you must all obey. When done, enfeoffment as marquis within the passes; disobedience exterminates three clans."

value.zh: 眾皆從之。
value.en: All obeyed.
value.literal: All obeyed.

value.zh: 又矯詔開門，夜入，陳兵道南，遣翊軍校尉齊王冏將百人排冏而入，華林令駱休為內應，迎帝幸東堂，以詔召賈謐於殿前，將誅之。
value.en: He forged orders to open the gates, entered at night, lined troops along the southern route, sent Sima Jiong, Prince of Qi, with a hundred men to force entry, Luo Xiu of Hualin as inside agent, escorted the emperor to the Eastern Hall, and summoned Jia Mi to execution.
value.literal: He also forged an edict to open the gates, entered by night, arrayed troops along the southern way, sent the Colonel of the Supports the Prince of Qi Sima Jiong with a hundred men to force the gates and enter, the Commandant of the Hualin Park Luo Xiu as inside agent, brought the emperor to the Eastern Hall, and by edict summoned Jia Mi before the hall to be executed.

value.zh: 謐走入西鐘下，呼曰：「阿后救我！」
value.en: Mi fled to the western bell-frame crying: "Mother, save me!"
value.literal: Mi ran beneath the western bell-frame crying: "Mother, save me!"

value.zh: 就斬之。
value.en: He was beheaded at once.
value.literal: He was beheaded on the spot.

value.zh: 賈后見齊王冏，驚曰：「卿何為來？」
value.en: Seeing Sima Jiong the empress cried: "Why are you here?"
value.literal: When Empress Jia saw Sima Jiong she exclaimed: "Why have you come?"

value.zh: 冏曰：「有詔收后。」
value.en: Jiong said: "An edict commands your arrest."
value.literal: Jiong said: "There is an edict to take the empress."

value.zh: 后曰：「詔當從我出，何詔也！」
value.en: She said: "Edicts should come from me—what edict is this!"
value.literal: The empress said: "Edicts should come from me—what edict is this!"

value.zh: 后至上閤，遙呼帝曰：「陛下有婦，使人廢之，亦行自廢矣。」
value.en: She climbed to the upper pavilion and called to the emperor: "You have a wife; when others depose her, you will be deposed yourself."
value.literal: She went up to the upper pavilion and called to the emperor from afar: "Your Majesty has a consort; when others deposed her, you too will be deposed."

value.zh: 是時，梁王肜亦預其謀，后問冏曰：「起事者誰？」
value.en: The Prince of Liang Sima Rong was also in the plot; she asked Jiong: "Who raised this?"
value.literal: At that time the Prince of Liang Sima Rong also took part in the plot; the empress asked Jiong: "Who raised the affair?"

value.zh: 冏曰：「梁、趙。」
value.en: Jiong said: "Liang and Zhao."
value.literal: Jiong said: "Liang and Zhao."

value.zh: 后曰：「系狗當繫頸，反系其尾，何得不然！」
value.en: She said: "Tie a dog by the neck, not the tail—was this not inevitable!"
value.literal: The empress said: "When tying a dog one should tie the neck—instead they tied the tail; how could it not turn out thus!"

value.zh: 遂廢后為庶人，幽之於建始殿，收趙粲、賈午等付暴室考竟。
value.en: She was deposed as a commoner and confined in the Jianshi Hall; Zhao Can, Jia Wu, and others were sent to the Severe Chamber for interrogation unto death.
value.literal: She was thereupon deposed as commoner and confined in the Jianshi Hall; Zhao Can, Jia Wu, and others were taken to the Severe Chamber for interrogation to the death.

value.zh: 詔尚書收捕賈氏親黨，召中書監、侍中、黃門侍郎、八座皆夜入殿。
value.en: An edict ordered arrest of the Jia clan; the Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, attendants, Yellow Gate Gentlemen, and Eight Seats were summoned at night.
value.literal: An edict ordered the Masters of Writing to arrest the Jia kin; the Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, attendants, Yellow Gate Gentlemen, and the Eight Seats were all summoned into the hall at night.

value.zh: 尚書始疑詔有詐，郎師景露版奏請手詔，倫等斬之以徇。
value.en: The Masters of Writing doubted the edict; Gentleman Shi Jing asked for the emperor's own hand; Lun beheaded him as warning.
value.literal: The Masters of Writing at first doubted the edict was false; Gentleman Shi Jing displayed the tablet and asked for a handwritten edict; Lun and the rest beheaded him as a warning.

value.event: Jia Wu and the empress refused the Han match and betrothed Wang Huifeng instead; no calendar date is stated.

value.descriptorSuggestion: Wife of Han Shou, Empress Jia's sister

value.event: Jia Wu blocked the Han marriage and plotted against the heir apparent

value.en: Jia Wu
